script.cite: BK4 printed p.85 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.91 (procedure); BK1 printed p.20 = book1.pdf PDF p.22 (dial: pointer at N = wiper on DN)
script.quote: [p.85:] To use the Decimal to Binary Converter: Enter any decimal number from 0 through 10 by turning the rotary switch to the desired position. The binary equivalent of the decimal number will appear in the binary output lights. (A light ON represents 1; a light OFF represents 0.) [BK1 p.20:] For example, when the pointer knob points at 1, the wiper arm makes an electrical connection between D1 and D16.

note: Printed claims only (Step 6). 49 wires, no errata (the errata sheet has no Book IV page 84 or 85 entry; image-read errata.pdf p.3); wire list image-read at 300 dpi from PDF p.91 and identical to the OCR list. Printed procedure (p.85): turn the rotary switch by hand to any decimal number 0-10; its binary equivalent appears in the binary output lights, ON = 1, OFF = 0. Only decimal 0 is asserted: binary 0 is every output light OFF, which does not depend on which light carries which bit. Positions 1-10 are entered in order, as the procedure invites, with no assert: p.84-85 never ties a lamp to a bit weight (programs.json printedUnprinted), so every nonzero pattern is derived and left to Step 7. The nearest printed basis for the lamp order is elsewhere in Book IV: p.72 (PDF p.78, 'Binary output lights 4, 5 and 6 will read OFF, OFF, ON or 001'), p.77 (PDF p.83, 'The answer will be displayed in binary output lights 3, 4, 5 and 6. For example, if lights 3 and 6 are ON and lights 4 and 5 are OFF, the answer is 1001 (9).') and p.79 (PDF p.85, 'light 4 is OFF, and lights 5 and 6 are ON. This is read as 011'), i.e. light 3 high order and light 6 low order on the same four lights this program wires; Tom's 2026-10-14 ruling (O-C12) covers Book IV's slide-switch LEFT=1 convention, not lamp order, and this program uses no slide switch. The final return to 0 is a script choice that re-checks 0 after relays 1-6 have operated (positions 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 drive coils); it goes by hand along the shortest path, and a 3 s dwell lets the lamps cool before the expect. Start dial position D0 is the construction state, restated by the first dialGrab. dialRelease then checks the dial stays at 0 without the hand.
